data.title: Wall Street climbs as investors await Anthropic debut
data.description:
The stock market moved higher on Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.

S&P 500 (SP500) +1.1%, the Dow (DJI) +0.4%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +1.9%.

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after pricing its IPO at $83 a share, above its expected range. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion, and its debut could offer a gauge of how public-market investors are assessing the longer-term commercial prospects of AI amid recent weakness in several AI-linked stocks.

Meanwhile, for the week ended Nov. 14, initial jobless claims in the U.S. rose by 1K to 203K, edging past the 198K consensus, according to data released by the U.S. Department of Labor.

On the other hand, Walmart (WMT) traded lower on Thursday, despite positive results, as investors assessed the retail giant's third-quarter earnings report and outlook for the holiday quarter.

data.title: NANO Nuclear, SJ Group sign MoU to pursue nuclear energy across Southeast Asia
data.description:
NANO Nuclear Energy (NNE) jumped 4.1% pre-market Thursday after saying it signed a memorandum of understanding with infrastructure developer SJ Group to pursue advanced nuclear energy in Southeast Asia and explore potential applications of NANO Nuclear's technologies in the region.

NANO Nuclear (NNE) said the collaboration combines SJ Group's established regional relationships and extensive engineering, planning, and project delivery capabilities with NANO Nuclear's KRONOS MMR Energy System to develop nuclear fuel supply capabilities and specialized nuclear transportation services.

The companies said they plan to focus initially on knowledge exchange and capability building, including technical exchanges on advanced nuclear technologies and their potential relevance to energy-intensive applications such as data centers and industrial facilities.

"Singapore and the broader Southeast Asian region represent potentially significant long-term markets for advanced nuclear energy, particularly as demand for reliable, carbon-free power continues to grow," NANO Nuclear (NNE) CEO James Walker said, adding that SJ Group's regional infrastructure expertise and project development experience make it a valuable partner.

data.title: Stocks to watch on Thursday: WMT, AMBA, WSM & more
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher early Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.

Here are the four stocks to watch on the day:

Walmart (WMT) traded 0.6% lower in premarket action on Thursday as investors assessed the retail giant's third-quarter results. The company reported adjusted EPS of $0.65, edging past the $0.64 consensus estimate, while U.S. comparable sales rose 2.9% versus expectations of 2.8%. U.S. e-commerce sales surged 23% during the quarter, with AI agents contributing to higher average basket sizes. Walmart raised its full-year revenue growth outlook to 4.9% to 5.2% and guided for EPS of $2.84 to $2.89.

Alibaba Group (BABA) edged down 2.1% in premarket trading after posting second-quarter results that showed revenue rising 10% year over year to 271.52 billion yuan ($40.5 billion), topping the 270.53 billion yuan consensus estimate. AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue jumped 53% to 60.97 billion yuan, exceeding expectations. However, non-GAAP net income of 19.91 billion yuan and adjusted earnings per ADS of 8.10 yuan both missed estimates as capital expenditure increased 60% to 50.48 billion yuan amid heavy AI infrastructure investment.

Williams-Sonoma (WSM) dropped more than 8% ahead of Thursday's open despite posting a 6% gain in total revenue to $1.99 billion, though results came in $10 million below expectations. Comparable store sales rose 5.1%, missing the 5.25% estimate, with the Pottery Barn banner lagging at 1.8% growth versus 5.1% expectations. Adjusted EPS of $2.19 matched estimates but was boosted by IEEPA tariff refunds that inflated gross margin by 140 basis points to 47.6%. The company maintained its full-year outlook for net revenue growth of 4.7% to 7.2%.

Ambarella (AMBA) soared 8.8% in premarket trading on reports that the company may be in the final stages of an acquisition by NXP Semiconductors (NXPI). Traders cited a Betaville "rare" alert indicating the two companies may have agreed to a price of between $95 and $100 per share, with Ambarella reportedly hiring bankers to provide a fairness opinion on the offer. NXP rose 3% on the news. Ambarella is scheduled to report third-quarter results on Tuesday.

data.title: Pay growth loses ground as inflation turns up the heat
data.description:
U.S. workers are losing purchasing power once again as resurgent inflation outpaces cooling wage growth across the domestic economy.

The Consumer Price Index climbed 3.7% year over year in September, eclipsing both the 3.1% annual increase in the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Cost Index and the 2.5% gain in Indeed's wage tracker, which is a three-month moving average.

That gap reverses a multi-year stretch from 2023 through 2025 in which pay growth largely beat moderating prices, leaving inflation-adjusted wages down 0.6% from a year earlier.

Consumer price growth, also well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, has reaccelerated this year mainly because conflict with Iran and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz triggered a spike in global energy prices. Lingering pass-through from 2025 trade tariffs on imported goods, as well as sticky shelter costs and heavy corporate investment in AI infrastructure have compounded those upward price pressures.

data.title: Bitcoin, crypto get a modest boost amid Anthropic bullishness
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) perked back up toward $64K on Thursday after dipping close to $62K overnight, as spirits brightened with Anthropic's (ANT) record-setting $81B IPO.

The appetite for the AI giant's IPO indicates there's still investor tolerance for risk after Nvidia's (NVDA) travails rattled markets late last week.

Bitcoin (BTC-USD), the oldest crypto and largest by market cap, rose 1.4% in the past 24 hours to $63.9K at 9:17 AM ET. 

The bullish vibes lifted smaller tokens as well as many crypto-linked stocks.

Ethereum (ETH-USD) gained 2.0% to $1.81K, XRP (XRP-USD) 0.5% to $0.99, solana (SOL-USD) 1.3% to $75.02, and Hyperliquid (HYPE-USD) 2.2% to $68.68.

In stocks, MARA Holdings (MARA) climbed 4.9%, Riot Platforms (RIOT) jumped 6.4%, Hut 8 (HUT) increased 6.0%, and CleanSpark (CLSK) advanced 5.3%.

 Galaxy Digital (GLXY) bounced up 6.6%, Coinbase Global (COIN) gained 3.5%, Circle Internet (CRCL) rose 3.6%, Strategy (MSTR) pulled up 3.5%, and Bakkt (BKKT) added 5.1%.

data.title: Russell 2000 registers first death cross in over a year
data.description:
The Russell 2000 (RTY), the primary gauge of U.S. small-cap stocks, formed a death cross on Wednesday as its 50-day moving average crossed below the 200-day moving average for the first time since March 2025.

The pattern is widely watched by technical analysts as a signal that a shorter-term decline has matured into a longer-term downtrend.

Historical results offer a mixed picture. In the 12 prior instances of a Russell 2000 death cross since 1987, the index stood higher 12 months later in 10 of those cases, according to data compiled by Daily Chartbook. Average forward returns have also been positive over that horizon.

Near-term price action has been less encouraging. After the March 2025 death cross, small-cap stocks declined roughly 16% over the subsequent two weeks before stabilizing.

Moving-average crossovers are lagging indicators by design; they confirm that weakness has already occurred rather than forecast the start of a new decline. Many technicians therefore treat them as trend-status markers rather than precise timing tools. 

Small-cap shares have underperformed larger-cap benchmarks in recent months amid tighter financial conditions and uneven economic data. The latest death cross arrives as the Russell 2000 trades below both its 50- and 200-day averages, consistent with the broader deterioration in market breadth observed since early autumn.

data.title: UBS, Swiss Bankers Association call for changes to final part of banking stability reforms - report
data.description:
UBS Group (UBS) and the Swiss Bankers Association have called for changes to the final part of the country's proposed banking stability reforms, Reuters reported on Thursday.

"The SBA firmly rejects an across-the-board tightening of regulations for the entire banking center and a disproportionate expansion of FINMA's powers," said the association in a statement released on Thursday.

FINMA, or the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority, is a Swiss government body responsible for financial regulation.

"An in-depth analysis of the legislative proposals and the Liquidity Ordinance shows that many measures do not have a clear link to the causes of the Credit Suisse crisis, nor do they make a proven additional contribution to financial stability," said SBA.

SBA said it considers the proposed banking stability reform as a whole to be excessive and unbalanced. 

The statement is a reaction to the conclusion of a public consultation on ​the new rules covering bank liquidity, resolution capacity, ⁠and the powers of FINMA.

"Substantial changes are needed to ensure that ‌additional ⁠requirements are limited to demonstrated risks, aligned with international standards and are proportionate in their overall impact," UBS reportedly said, noting that an assessment of the cumulative costs of all the ​so-called too-big-to-fail measures ​is still ⁠lacking.

data.title: Russell 2000 forms death cross; stocks could see double-digit declines over the coming weeks
data.description:
The Russell 2000 Index (IWM) formed a “Death cross” on Wednesday.

 

 

 

This happens when a short-term moving average, the 50-day moving average, drops below the 200-day moving average, signaling that recent price momentum has weakened and a longer downtrend may occur.

The last time a death cross formed in the Russell 2000’s (IWM) trendline—in March 2025—stocks tumbled 16% over the following two weeks.

Small caps (IWM) have advanced 9.72% year-to-date, are down 0.29% from a month ago, and ended +0.4% on Wednesday.

The index closed $270.12, with its 50-day and 200-day moving averages crossing the $279 range.

data.title: Deutsche Bank raises 2027 dollar outlook on AI support
data.description:
Deutsche Bank has lifted its dollar (DXY) forecasts for 2027, outlining a “higher for longer” path that breaks with historical mean-reversion patterns. It expects further gains into the first half of next year, then only modest softening in the second half, leaving the currency still elevated.

The investment bank noted that the AI capital-expenditure boom remains the dominant force. It has pushed U.S. real rates higher, drawn heavy equity inflows, revived inflation pressures, and kept the Federal Reserve relatively hawkish. As a result, the United States is set to regain leadership in both yield and growth. The dollar’s return as a high-yielder, alongside a sharp compression in rate spreads versus emerging-market currencies, supports strength even under the bank’s base case of solid global growth and risk appetite. 

This year’s resilience has already illustrated the theme. Weakness failed to materialize, and the dollar could have been stronger still given the oil shock and French political risk. Offsets included robust global expansion, large U.S. twin deficits, softer fixed-income inflows, and relative strength in the Chinese yuan. On balance, the “AI dollar” holds. 

Risks are building though Deutsche Bank added. Growing reliance on AI spending leaves the dollar vulnerable to any material downgrade in capital-expenditure plans, which would likely lower real rates and curb equity inflows. Recent technology equity weakness has not yet weighed on the currency, as Fed pricing stays elevated. Rotation into bonds appears unlikely to provide lasting support amid signs of flows shifting from treasuries to foreign fixed-income markets.
